cityWatch.label: CITY WATCH
cityWatch.text: Bengaluru South civic teams say 143 abandoned vehicles have been towed after notices; another 110 are still marked for removal. The drive covered roadsides and footpaths across several divisions.
cityWatch.attribution: — Bengaluru South City Corporation / Urban Acres

lead.headline: BDA CUTS REGULARISATION FEES BY HALF FOR OLDER HOMES
lead.deck: Karnataka’s new measure covers eligible homes built before 2008 on BDA-acquired land; residents have until December 17 to apply
paragraphs: The Karnataka government has cut by half the regularisation charges for eligible homes built before 2008 on land acquired by the Bangalore Development Authority. Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said the measure could benefit more than one lakh Bengaluru residents.

The revised fees are 5%, 12.5%, 20% or 25% of the guidance value, depending on the plot size, and applications may be made online or in person. The deadline is December 17, 2026; applicants must provide proof of possession.
The announcement also includes measures for existing BDA site owners and farmers who voluntarily surrendered land.

sidebarStory.headline: PAWAN KALYAN AND ANNA KONIDELA ANNOUNCE SEPARATION
sidebarStory.subhead: The actor and Andhra Pradesh deputy chief minister said in a joint statement that they will remain devoted parents
paragraphs: Pawan Kalyan and Anna Konidela have announced that their marriage has ended after 13 years. Their joint statement described the decision as mutual and said they would continue to support their children; it gave no reason for the separation.

stories.headline: CITY TO HOST FIRST COMMONWEALTH WOMEN PARLIAMENTARIANS CONFERENCE IN INDIA
paragraphs: Bengaluru will host the first standalone Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians India Region Conference on November 17 and 18. About 150 women legislators and delegates from 15–20 countries are expected to discuss leadership and online harms including cyber abuse and deepfakes.

image.alt: Karnataka legislature leaders announcing the Bengaluru conference at Vidhana Soudha
image.caption: Assembly Speaker G S Patil and Council Chair Saleem Ahmed at the announcement. Photo: The New Indian Express

stories.headline: DEVELOPER AND BORROWERS ACCUSED OF MULTI-CRORE BANK FRAUD
paragraphs: Police complaints by State Bank of India allege that a Bengaluru developer and borrowers used fictitious buyers and inflated flat valuations to obtain loans. The complaints cite alleged losses of ₹4.88 crore and ₹5.55 crore; the allegations have not been adjudicated.

stories.headline: 143 ABANDONED VEHICLES REMOVED FROM ROADS AND FOOTPATHS
paragraphs: Bengaluru South civic authorities removed 143 vehicles after a seven-day notice period, following a joint drive with traffic police. Officials had identified 595 vehicles; another 110 remain marked for towing, while 195 were reclaimed after owners paid fines.

groups.ariaLabel: India courts, diplomacy, and pilgrimage news

stories.headline: HIGH COURT KEEPS MANIPUR CENSUS ON HOLD UNTIL APRIL 2027
paragraphs: The Manipur High Court directed the Centre to keep the Census 2027 exercise in the state on hold until April 30, 2027, while authorities consider concerns raised amid ethnic violence and displacement. It asked the Census Commissioner to decide seven representations and allowed further submissions through November 25.

stories.headline: MODI AND ZELENSKYY DISCUSS PEACE EFFORTS AND BILATERAL TIES
paragraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke by phone with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on November 9. Modi reiterated India’s support for a resolution through dialogue and diplomacy, and the leaders discussed strengthening bilateral cooperation.

stories.headline: INDIA SECURES HAJ QUOTA OF 1,75,025 PILGRIMS FOR 2027
paragraphs: India and Saudi Arabia signed their bilateral Haj agreement for 2027, setting India’s quota at 1,75,025 pilgrims. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju met Saudi Minister of Hajj and Umrah Tawfiq bin Fawzan Al Rabiah in Jeddah before the agreement was signed.

groups.ariaLabel: India justice and public life news

stories.headline: SC ASKS UP TO FIND PRISONERS STILL JAILED AFTER GETTING BAIL
paragraphs: The Supreme Court directed Uttar Pradesh to identify undertrial prisoners who remain in jail despite being granted bail, in consultation with District Legal Services Authorities. The bench said the state must ensure their release and called for bail orders to reach jails promptly through email and the e-prisons system.

stories.headline: SIX OF FAMILY DIE IN DIWALI-NIGHT HOUSE FIRE IN DHARASHIV
paragraphs: Six members of a family died after a fire swept through their home and grocery shop in Yedshi village, Maharashtra, on Diwali night. A teenager survived; authorities are investigating the cause, while villagers alleged that the fire tender arrived late.

stories.headline: DELHI PREPARES MORE THAN 1,400 GHATS FOR CHHATH PUJA
paragraphs: Delhi is preparing more than 1,400 ghats and an 11-kilometre stretch of the Munak Canal for Chhath Puja. The city’s arrangements are being put in place ahead of the festival, which draws large gatherings of devotees.

stories.headline: INDIA TAKE 2–0 LEAD INTO THIRD ODI IN HAMILTON
paragraphs: India face New Zealand in the third one-day international in Hamilton on Tuesday, with the visitors leading the five-match series 2–0 after close wins in Auckland and Wellington. The match is scheduled for 7:30 a.m. India time at Seddon Park.

stories.headline: IMD FORECASTS A DRY, PARTLY CLOUDY TUESDAY
paragraphs: The India Meteorological Department forecast partly cloudy skies in Bengaluru on Tuesday, with a minimum temperature of 20°C and a maximum of 29°C. No warning is in effect for the city.
